# John Meredith

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male
- **Status:** Alive
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island, Canada
- **Role:** Presbyterian Minister
- **Titles:** Reverend

## Appearance

John Meredith is a tall, scholarly-looking man with a gentle and dreamily handsome face. He has dark, absent-minded eyes that often seem fixed on spiritual or intellectual matters rather than his immediate surroundings. His demeanor is quiet, refined, and deeply reflective.

## Personality

Reverend Meredith is a deeply pious, learned, and gentle man, but he is notoriously absent-minded and impractical in day-to-day affairs. He often becomes completely absorbed in his theological studies and books, leaving him oblivious to household disorganization and the mischief of his children. Though he loves his children dearly, his unworldly nature makes him hesitant and ineffective at disciplining them. He possesses a delicate sensitivity, a kind heart, and a sincere desire to be a good pastor and father.

## Traits

- Absent-minded
- Scholarly and scholarly-minded
- Gentle and soft-spoken
- Impractical in domestic matters
- Pious and dedicated to his faith

## Abilities

- Theological scholarship and preaching
- Classical learning and reading

## Goals

- To faithfully serve his congregation in Glen St. Mary
- To raise his motherless children well despite his practical shortcomings

## History

Following the death of his beloved wife, Cecilia, Reverend John Meredith accepts the call to become the Presbyterian minister at Glen St. Mary, moving into the manse with his four children—Jerry, Faith, Una, and Thomas Carlyle—and his elderly aunt, Aunt Martha. Devastated by his loss and absorbed in his books, he inadvertently neglects the practical oversight of his household and children. The neglected Meredith children form a close friendship with Anne and Gilbert Blythe's children at Rainbow Valley. After gossip in the village regarding his children's wild antics reaches him, John realizes his shortcomings as a father and strives to pay more attention to their upbringing. Over time, he realizes that his household needs a mother's touch and falls in love with Rosemary West. Although their courtship faces initial obstacles due to a pact between Rosemary and her sister Ellen, the issues are resolved, and John marries Rosemary West.

## Background by volume

- Was happily married to Cecilia (Cissy), who died, leaving him a grieving widower with four young children
- Moved to Glen St. Mary to accept the call as minister of the Presbyterian church at the manse

- Glen St. Mary Presbyterian Church — Minister
